summary: Decision table separating agent noun, stable-quality adjective and intensive form when they share one surface template, keyed on source-verb transitivity, degree semantics and complement behaviour.
why_existing_insufficient: the ambiguity spans two proposed units and u-s03, so no single unit can own it; without a discriminator any class assignment on a shared template is a guess.

summary: given a verb and a following nominative nominal, decide whether the nominal is the agent or the deputy agent, listing the evidence each decision requires and marking the cases that are undecidable without vocalisation
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 states that a verb governs its subject but does not distinguish the two subject roles, and u-n01 marks nominative case without saying which role earned it; in unvocalised text this discrimination is exactly where a reader silently guesses

summary: A consistency check that, given a head noun with a number, a referent class and a word order, verifies that every dependent verb, adjective, demonstrative and clitic in the clause carries a licensed agreement form, and abstains where the referent of a clitic is undetermined.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 stores number and gender morphology and u-s09 stores clitic layering, but neither checks agreement across categories in one clause, and u-n10 covers referent attachment without encoding the word-order and referent-class conditions that license or block agreement here.

summary: Licensing table whose rows are keyed on the linear position of a controller relative to its target, returning which agreement features (gender only, or gender and number) are exponed on the target, with the verb-before-agent versus agent-before-verb pair as the first two rows.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 supplies the gender and number exponents themselves and u-n03 records that the verb governs its agent, but neither conditions the choice of exponent on linear order, which is exactly what decides correctness here.

summary: A four-way discriminator for the short subordinating particle: role label, required left context, required right context, and the mood/governance consequence of each role, with the substitution and deletion tests as secondary criteria.
why_existing_insufficient: The catalog's multifunction-particle unit is scoped by its label to ما; no listed unit carries a role inventory or evidence table for this particle, and the mood-assignment consequence is not derivable from the general case+mood unit alone.

summary: Inventory of named meters, their constituent feet, per-hemistich repetition counts, mora totals, and the licence system that permits specified deviations; declared instructional_only because no registered capability accepts syllable-weight strings as input.
why_existing_insufficient: no catalogued unit models syllable weight, hemistich structure or metrical templates; the morphological template unit classifies derivational patterns over roots, which is a different template space with different primitives, and treating them as one would be domain resemblance rather than coverage

summary: The directive, commitment and status-conferral readings of assertive clauses, retained as teaching material with their indicator checklists but explicitly not projectable.
why_existing_insufficient: Their decisive features are authority relations and discourse stakes, which no consumer-backed capability family can represent.

summary: A named taxonomy of purposes an assertive utterance can serve, together with the situational cues the tradition associates with each, held explicitly as teaching material rather than as a projection capability.
why_existing_insufficient: No catalog unit ranges over utterance purpose, and the substance cannot be reduced to any of the five consumer-backed capability families because its decisive features are extralinguistic.

summary: check that a coordinated element's observed case marking equals the marking of the element it is joined to, abstaining when either marking is unknown or when the connector's reading is not coordination
why_existing_insufficient: the registered pattern_consistency analyzer is keyed to abrogator families with ism and khabar slots; a تابع/متبوع comparison needs a generic head-and-dependent marking input that this shape cannot express

summary: Per-occurrence discriminator for the coordination particle set: for each form, separates the coordinating use from its homographic non-coordinating uses using position between two terms, case identity, polarity of the preceding clause, and the size of the following unit, with an attributed no-decision path for the two disputed members.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 already establishes the multifunction-particle problem but is scoped to one form; this lesson adds a whole family of forms whose coordinating and non-coordinating senses are distinguished by different evidence, and u-n11 records rival analyses without providing the per-occurrence test.

summary: A discriminator for the attention, topic-setting, presentative and surprise particles, keyed to position, prefix attachment and the category of the following constituent, including the two near-homograph minimal pairs.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 is built around multifunction particle disambiguation but is anchored on a different item; u-n06 covers conditional structure and u-n12 covers discourse cohesion, yet no unit in the catalog carries the attention and presentative particle class or the positional test that splits the two readings of the conditional-looking element.

summary: Licensing table for the attributive descriptive follower: given head features plus a referent animacy label, it states the required modifier features, and given an annexation chain it states which case realises which attachment, including an explicit undecidable outcome when both chain members share a case.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n10 addresses attachment, scope and referent but carries no agreement-axis licensing check, and u-s08 supplies number and gender morphology without the syntactic condition under which the two must match

summary: Decision table for an adjacent nominal pair sharing a case: routes to total, partitive, inclusion, or corrective apposition, keyed on presence of a resumptive clitic, referential identity, and a part-versus-containment judgement, with an explicit shared-label outcome where total apposition and appositional clarification are formally indistinguishable.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n05 covers the resumptive link inside relative clauses only, and u-n10 records attachment and referent without a typology; nothing in the catalog states when a clitic is obligatory on a nominal follower or how the four apposition readings are told apart.

summary: Discriminator for a referentially identical adjacent nominal pair that must be able to return both labels: it applies the shared formal checks (case, definiteness, rigid versus derived second member), then reports apposition, appositional clarification, or both-licensed with the attribution attached, rather than forcing a single winner.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n11 stores rival and school analyses as a record but supplies no per-occurrence routine, and every other candidate unit assumes a decidable label; this pair is formally undecidable, which is a different requirement from a hard case.

summary: Feature-driven separation of ornamentation figures (sound-resemblance pairing, contrariety pairing, and their polarity and completeness subtypes) using boolean features such as form resemblance, sense opposition, polarity of members and vocalisation identity, with abstention preserved when features are insufficient or several figures survive.
why_existing_insufficient: no catalogued unit addresses span-level rhetorical figures at all; the morphology units cover form derivation and the syntax units cover government and structure, neither of which decides whether two co-occurring tokens stand in a rhetorical relation

summary: A discriminator table for the bound proclitic connector that separates its functions — immediate sequence, direct consequence, apodosis marking after a conditional, causative use forcing the subjunctive, and resumptive use — with the contextual evidence that selects each.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 is scoped to multifunction particles exemplified by a different item and carries no entry for this proclitic; u-n12 records discourse relations without the syntactic licensing that separates apodosis marking from mere sequence; u-n06 supplies the conditional context but not the discrimination procedure. This module teaches four of the proclitic's functions in four separate lessons with no single place that tells them apart, which is precisely a discriminator_table gap.

summary: A boundary-level table stating when two adjacent vowelless consonants arise across a token boundary and which repair applies: the trigger inventory of connective initial hamzas, the repair vowel per ending type, the licensed deletion cases, and the pause versus connection switch that gates the whole thing.
why_existing_insufficient: Every sarf unit in the catalogue is word-internal and every nahw unit is structural; none takes a pair of adjacent tokens as its input. u-s07 covers weak-letter alternation and replacement inside a word, not junctural repair, and u-n12 concerns discourse cohesion rather than phonological delivery.

summary: Inventory mapping singular templates to attested restructured-plural templates, with per-lexeme overrides, multiple attested plurals, and recognition signatures for classifying an unseen plural token.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 records that number is marked and how; it carries no template inventory and no many-to-many singular-to-plural mapping, which is what both classification and validation of a restructured plural require.

summary: A decision table that maps a pronominal clitic plus its host category to a single role reading (verbal complement, possessor in annexation, or complement of a governing particle) together with the positional case that follows.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers the layering of clitics onto stems and u-n03 covers governance in general, but neither provides the host-category-to-role decision that a per-occurrence annotator needs when the same suffix shape is ambiguous between object and possessor.

summary: Assigns a noun to generic collective, derived unit noun, unit-less collective, or ordinary singular-with-broken-plural, and records for each class the licensed number morphology and the admissible agreement patterns with their register weighting.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 handles number and gender morphology on ordinary nouns; it has no class for a singular-shaped noun with plural reference, no unit-extraction relation, and no representation of agreement optionality conditioned on that class.

summary: an index from each Arabic grammatical label to its ordinary sense, its function slot, and its case requirement, so that commentary prose can be decoded label by label
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog units encode the phenomena, not the label inventory used to talk about them; nothing carries a term-to-function mapping, and no capability family with a real consumer covers a glossary, so this is honestly instructional rather than a consumer capability

summary: A licensing table keyed by connective that records, for each contrastive, concessive and causal connective, the complement shape it admits (accusative nominal plus predicate, أنّ-clause, genitive noun phrase, or bare clause) and the case or mood it forces on the immediately following element.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n02 covers the inna family as a closed morphosyntactic class and does not extend to prepositional frames or compound markers; u-n03 states the general notion of government without a per-connective complement inventory; u-n12 treats cohesion at discourse level and carries no case or complement information. The licensing information here cuts across all three and is exactly the shape a licensing_table consumer needs.

summary: Table stating, for each clause configuration, whether a constituent may, must, or must not precede its default position, keyed on the category of the moved constituent, the definiteness of the topic, the type of the predicate, and the presence of an interrogative, exclamatory, or detached-pronoun trigger, with a companion rule that the moved constituent retains its role case and may require a resumptive pronoun.
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog has no unit about linear order: u-n01 assigns case once roles are known, u-n10 tracks referents and scope but not permissibility of position, and u-n11 records rival analyses without stating which orders are licensed.

summary: a closed two-way classification of the letter inventory deciding whether the definite article's laam assimilates, together with the gemination it produces on the following consonant
why_existing_insufficient: the nearest catalog unit covers stem-internal weak-letter change; assimilation across a clitic boundary is a different process over a different closed set, and no listed unit represents the article's phonological behaviour at all

summary: Licensing table mapping each source of definiteness (article, proper name, closed definite classes, annexation to a definite) to the surface evidence that establishes it and to the surface evidence that would otherwise be misleading, so that a definiteness verdict is issued by source rather than by marker.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers how clitics and inflectional layers stack on a surface but does not adjudicate definiteness, and u-n01 consumes definiteness without deriving it; nothing in the catalog blocks the nunation-means-indefinite inference that this lesson's own examples falsify.

summary: A licensing table keyed on demonstrative plus following nominal that returns the phrase reading when the nominal is definite and the predication reading when it is indefinite, together with the agreement conditions (gender, number, rationality) that must hold for each.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n10 covers attachment and referent resolution and u-n09 covers positional case, but neither encodes the definiteness switch that decides whether a demonstrative sequence is a noun phrase or a complete sentence, which is the single most consequential decision this construction forces.

summary: A per-root and per-semantic-field admissibility gate answering whether a given root may realize a given augmented verb pattern at all: the first-radical gap set that blocks the ن-prefix pattern, and the closed semantic fields that alone license the final-gemination pattern.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s02 as catalogued enumerates and describes the pattern series; the substance here is not what a pattern looks like but whether a root is admitted to it, which is a licensing decision consumed before any template is applied. If u-s02 already carries an admissibility table rather than only form descriptions, this folds into u-s02 instead of standing alone.

summary: A table stating when an object pronoun must appear in the detached accusative series rather than as a clitic, keyed on position relative to the verb and on whether another element already occupies the attachment site, together with the full series paradigm.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers clitic and pronoun layering on a host word but has no entry for the detached series or for the conditions that force it, and u-n10 handles referent attachment without licensing the pronoun's form.

summary: Classifies a noun base for diminution (consonant count, medial length, affix inventory, covert gender, compound headedness) and maps the class to its diminutive output template, keeping the inserted glide and skeleton vowels out of the root.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s01 owns letter attribution and u-s06/u-s07 own weak-class and substitution behaviour, but none of them holds a diminutive base-class to template mapping, and the affix and compound-name conditions have no home in the catalog.

summary: A licensing table for nunation blocking: feature pairs and template families that block, the definiteness and construct conditions that cancel blocking, and a register-gated override row for verse.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 holds the default case-exponent system and u-s08 holds number and gender morphology; neither encodes a trigger-pair licensing decision that overrides the default exponent for a whole lexeme class.

summary: The suspension side of the reduced-exponent class: which environments restore the ordinary case vowel, which restore nothing, and which term of an annexation is affected.
why_existing_insufficient: cu-diptote-cause-licensing decides membership only; nothing in the catalog encodes an environment-triggered override that switches a lexeme back to the default exponent for the duration of one occurrence.

summary: Licensing table for the three comparison constructions, recording which one permits agreement, which freezes the elative in the masculine singular, that the definite and annexed constructions exclude the comparison complement, and what evidence each construction requires before a degree reading is asserted.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 records that markings need governors but holds no construction inventory for comparison, and u-n01 assigns case only once the construction is identified. The mutual exclusion of definiteness and the comparison complement is a construction-level restriction with no home in the catalog.

summary: Decision table separating the elative reading of the أَفعَل shape from its homographs — the colour and bodily-defect adjective of the same shape, the fourth-form perfect verb, and the first-person singular imperfect — keyed on the availability of a comparison complement, definiteness behaviour, which feminine counterpart template the lexeme takes, and root and entry evidence.
why_existing_insufficient: The catalog contains no unit for elatives, and the committed capability matrix files them under a family whose instructional support is recorded as pending. u-s02 classifies verb forms and u-s08 handles number and gender, but neither decides which part of speech an أَفعَل-shaped token instantiates, and the rival readings differ in part of speech rather than in nuance.

summary: A table stating, for each emphasis device, what category it attaches to, in what position, and what co-occurrence it requires: the emphatic lam licensed on the predicate of the emphatic particle or under the oath-lam; the emphatic nun licensed on jussive/subjunctive verbs with an obligatory fatḥa; قد licensed pre-verbally with aspect-dependent readings.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n02 covers the nasikh particles' governance and u-s09 covers inflectional layering, but neither records cross-device attachment licensing or the co-occurrence stacking that this lesson makes central.

summary: Letter-level feature table recording emphatic and heavy membership, the plain counterpart of each emphatic, and the minimal pairs that establish the contrast.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s01 concerns whether a letter belongs to the root, the pattern, or an affix, which is a different notion of letter property, and no existing unit records segmental phonological features.

summary: A licensing and attachment table for the emphatic verb suffix: which contexts require it, which permit it, which persons and numbers admit each shape, what deletes on attachment, what residual vowel remains as the person trace, and how the result is told apart from the feminine plural ending.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers clitic and pronoun layering, and this suffix is neither a clitic pronoun nor an inflectional ending of the ordinary paradigm; u-n01 covers case and mood but not a suffix that suspends mood marking. Neither unit expresses the person-and-number-keyed deletion table or the shape restriction, and without them a parser cannot recover the person of a suffixed form.

summary: Maps each reading of the connective proclitic to its triggering environment and to the mood it licenses or leaves untouched on a following imperfect verb, including the cases where more than one mood is licit.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 is scoped to a different multifunction particle and u-n01 states the mood system without the trigger-to-reading mapping that makes the mood predictable here.

summary: Records the unresolved boundary between one-token polysemy figures and two-token resemblance figures as taught across this module, keeping both attributions attached to their source lessons rather than silently choosing one.
why_existing_insufficient: the conflict is between two lessons of the same module rather than between schools of grammar, so it does not belong under the rival-analyses syntax unit, and it must not be collapsed into a single ruling by an automatic consumer

summary: A discriminator assigning a noun to one of three stem-final classes from its citation shape, with the resulting definiteness-by-case exponent behaviour and the near-miss shapes that must be excluded.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 groups weak, hamzated and doubled roots and u-s07 covers the sound changes, but neither yields a surface-shape discriminator that predicts whether a case exponent will be visible, deleted or covert.

summary: Closed-list table gating the long-vowel case-exponent series by number, annexation state and the identity of the annexed element, with the fallback short-exponent forms.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 holds the default exponent inventory, u-s09 holds clitic layering and u-s06 holds weak-radical classes, but none of them gates an alternative exponent series on a three-part configuration test for a closed lexical list.

summary: Classification of prefix-conjugated verbs into the vowel-exponed set, the closed nun-bearing set whose mood exponent is a retained or deleted letter, and the fixed-shape feminine-plural set that does not alternate for mood at all.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 names letter endings only for duals, sound plurals and the five nouns; the five verbs are a distinct verbal class whose exponent is a letter, and the feminine-plural form must be excluded from mood alternation entirely, neither of which the catalog states.

summary: An enumerable inventory of fixed-form nominal tokens keyed to surface shape, recording each item's invariant final vowel, its category, and the case slots it may occupy, with the annexation-conditioned exception marked.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers clitic and inflection layering and u-n09 covers estimated structure in the abstract, but neither provides a token-keyed inventory that a per-occurrence consumer could look up to decide that no exponent will ever appear.

summary: Decision table separating the Form I agent and patient participles of one root using letter-level evidence alone — presence of the م augment, position of the long vowel, and radical order — so that voice can be assigned in unvowelled text where no penult vowel is available, with the hollow, initial-hamza and doubled outcomes recorded as licensed variants rather than failures.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s03's only recorded contrast is the penult-vowel discriminator for the م-prefixed participles of the derived forms. That test is inapplicable to Form I, where the two participles differ by consonantal skeleton rather than by a short vowel, and u-s03 lists the weak-root outcomes only as an undifferentiated exception.

summary: A licensing table for verbless clauses whose predicate is a fronted locative or benefactive phrase, returning the delayed-subject reading and its nominative case, the condition under which an indefinite subject is licensed, and the effect of each negating operator on the frame.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 supplies the case system and u-n08 covers deleted or implicit structure, but neither encodes the fronting-licenses-indefinite-subject condition that makes this whole construction well formed, and without it the possessed nominal is routinely misread as an object.

summary: Holds a closed list of invariant multi-word documentary formulas and marks them as non-compositional units, so that a parser or glosser treats them whole rather than deriving a misleading word-by-word reading.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n12 covers cohesion devices as productive grammar; these formulas are lexically frozen items whose interpretation is institutional rather than compositional, which no existing unit is scoped to record.

summary: enumerate the licensed jussive realisations of a geminate stem and mark which surface strings are mood forms and which are indicatives, so that a reader or grader accepts every licensed shape and rejects only the unlicensed one
why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 classifies the stem and u-n01 treats mood exponence for sound stems as a single expected shape per cell; neither carries a cell with several correct realisations, which is exactly what this class requires

summary: A table stating, per environment, whether consonant merger is required, blocked, or optional: identical consonants with the first vowelless, consonant-initial person suffixes, reflexive-augment assimilation, emphatic conditioning, and cross-boundary contexts.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 classifies the final-geminate root class but does not encode the environment-by-environment licensing decision, and u-s07 covers weak-letter alternation and letter replacement rather than gemination; nothing in the catalogue answers the question of whether a given cell must, may, or must not geminate.

summary: the closed letter inventory together with skeleton families, dot signatures, and the resulting set of confusable letter pairs
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog begins at root/pattern/affix letter ownership and silently assumes the grapheme layer is already settled; no listed unit represents letter identity, dot signatures, or confusability

summary: A licensing table for the accusative state role keyed on three independent conditions — definiteness of the state-holder, presence or absence of the connective by realisation type, and presence of a coreferent linking pronoun — together with the exclusion tests against coordination, attribution, and adverbial complementation.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n04 enumerates accusative roles and u-n09 supplies positional case, but neither encodes the conjunction of licensing conditions that must all hold before this particular role may be assigned, nor the exclusion tests that make the assignment safe.

summary: given the vowel environment and the position of a hamza, list the licensed written carriers for it, so that variant spellings of one token are recognised as the same word rather than as different entries
why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 classifies hamzated stems and u-s07 states morphological substitutions; neither addresses the written carrier, and carrier variation is a spelling-level fact that a corpus index meets on every hamza-bearing token

summary: a deterministic selection of the written seat for the glottal stop from position plus the ranked vowels of its environment, with the seatless and combined-grapheme cases
why_existing_insufficient: the nearest catalog unit covers hamzated roots as a morphological class; it does not encode the orthographic seat, and it is exactly the spelling variation this unit describes that breaks naive surface matching to those roots

summary: given the ambiguous purpose-or-limit particle before a verb, decide the intended reading and the licensed mood, and record which readings are compatible with a prospective versus an attained event
why_existing_insufficient: the multifunction-particle unit is scoped to a different item, and the governance unit does not encode a mapping in which the mood and the semantic reading determine each other

summary: Selector predicting, for a hollow lexeme in a given environment, whether the medial vowel is retained or shortened and which short vowel results, taking the certified weak radical together with the underlying pattern vowel as inputs and abstaining where the pattern vowel is unrecorded.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 assigns the weak class and warns against reading the long alif as a radical, and u-s07 owns transformation chains in general, but neither records the pattern vowel that decides the shortened quality, which is the one input the surface cannot supply.

summary: An adjacency constraint on the construct expressed as a licensing table: required in prose, relaxable in verse for listed interposer classes under a stated motive, plus a recovery procedure for a delayed complement.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 covers government and u-n10 covers attachment and scope, but neither encodes adjacency as a violable constraint with an enumerated relaxation set, and neither can gate that relaxation on register.

summary: Position-indexed licensing of article, tanwin, and case across the nodes of a construct chain of arbitrary depth, including the rule that the head's case comes from outside the chain.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 states construct government for a two-term pair but not the position-indexed definiteness and case licensing that a chain of depth n requires.

summary: Licensing table for annexation: which exponents the head may not carry (tanwin, the definite article, and the dual and sound-plural final consonant), the invariant genitive on the dependent, definiteness inheritance from the final member, the chain rule that only the last member may carry a definiteness exponent, and the participial subtype recorded as the licensed exception that both admits the article on the head and blocks definiteness inheritance.
why_existing_insufficient: The committed capability matrix files annexation as a family with no instructional support and no fixtures, and names an annexation unit as remaining work. u-n03 lists the construct head as one governor type but carries no construction-internal rules; u-n01 marks case without the definiteness and exponent-suppression facts. Neither can decide whether an adjacent noun pair is an annexation at all.

summary: Discriminator that classifies a construct by the derivational class of its head and the rephrasing test, and records the definiteness consequences that follow from the class.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 states construct government without distinguishing the two types, and u-s03 supplies participle morphology without the syntactic consequence of a participle heading a construct.

summary: A table licensing bare accusative exhortative nouns, keyed on polarity of the named target, on repetition or coordination, and on the presence of a detached pronoun plus conjunction, and naming the estimated imperative for each frame.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n04 lists accusative categories without licensing conditions for verbless exhortation, and u-n08 covers estimated material without distinguishing the two exhortative frames or their pronoun requirements.

summary: A table licensing the case of a group-naming noun that interrupts a pronoun and its predicate, keyed on definiteness, on the presence of the introducing particle and on the person of the pronoun, and separating the construction from the vocative and from apposition.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n04 enumerates accusative categories but holds no licensing conditions for this one, and u-n08 covers estimated material without stating which surface configurations trigger this particular estimation.

summary: A table keyed on the linear position of a mental-state verb relative to its two candidate complements, emitting whether accusative assignment is required, optional or withheld, with the preference grading kept attributed.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 treats governance as a property of the governor rather than of its position, and u-n01 records case and mood outcomes without any positional conditioning.

summary: A discriminator that separates assertive from enacting readings of a clause using surface-checkable features (head particle identity, imperative/jussive marking, first-person performative verb class, embedding under a knowledge verb) and explicitly abstains where only speaker-authority context could decide.
why_existing_insufficient: The catalog units cover morphology, case/mood, governance and particle polysemy, but none assigns an utterance-level force label or records where force is underdetermined by form.

summary: A span-level consistency check over person, number and tense features for a constant referent, which flags a licensed break, records its dimension and direction, and separates a licensed break from an agreement error by requiring referent constancy.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n12 gains genuinely new material here, namely that cohesion can be maintained across a deliberate break in framing and that the break itself is a cohesion signal; u-n10 gains the case where person changes without a referent change; u-s09 is only consumed, since the inflectional layering is used as evidence and not taught. What none of them carries is the span-level consistency check plus the licensed-exception clause, which is what makes the phenomenon checkable.

summary: Derivation procedure taking a prefix-conjugated verb to its command form: third-mood stem, prefix removal, conditional prosthetic alif with a stem-computed vowel, pattern and weak-radical exceptions, and an explicit non-radical marking on the prosthetic element.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s01 owns letters as root, pattern or affix but has no derivation that introduces a letter belonging to none of the three; u-s02 classifies derived forms without deriving command stems from them; u-s06 covers weak classes but not the prosthetic step they interact with.

summary: Decision table assigning every word-initial alif to the connecting or the cutting class from word category, derived-pattern membership, letter count and closed-list membership, with an abstention branch for unpointed text where the assignment is lexical inference rather than observation.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s01 owns letters as root, pattern or affix but has no category for a prosthetic element that is dropped in connected speech; u-s02 classifies derived forms without linking them to hamza behaviour; u-s09 peels the article as a proclitic without deciding the class of its initial alif.

summary: which member of the particle family is licensed in which environment — clause-initial, selected by a preceding cognition or speech verb, or adversative — together with the geminate versus non-geminate test that decides whether an occurrence governs at all
why_existing_insufficient: inc-nawasikh already contemplates a non-governing use through its abstention reason, but supplies no criterion for detecting one; this lesson supplies exactly that criterion for the adversative member and adds positional criteria the increment lacks entirely

summary: modal force carried by each member of the particle family — emphasis, subordination, adversative contrast, resemblance, counterfactual wish, attainable hope — as a gloss-facing field held separately from the governance field
why_existing_insufficient: u-n02 and inc-nawasikh record only what each member does to case, so a hover or tutor surface built from them would present six members as if they were six spellings of one thing; the unit is deliberately marked instructional_only because no current consumer can act on it

summary: Template inventory for intensive and habitual agent forms, recording degree semantics, the non-gender taa, and each template's competing class assignments.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s03 covers participles as such and carries no degree dimension; u-s02 covers verb forms, not deverbal adjective templates; nothing existing records that a template can belong to two adjective classes at once.

summary: A keyed table assigning case to a noun standing before a verb that governs a coreferential clitic, conditioned on the left-peripheral particle and on whether the verb could have governed that noun directly.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 records that governors assign case but holds no keyed decision table for this displaced-argument configuration, and u-n08 covers estimated unpronounced material without selecting the resulting case.

summary: A discriminator deciding, for a non-literal expression, whether a pole is genuinely deleted and which one, using the presence of an alien-field clue plus a check that no second pole occurs in the span.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n08 covers structure that is syntactically absent but grammatically recorded, such as governed gaps and estimated elements with case consequences; here nothing is recorded in the parse and the missing pole is recovered by world knowledge alone, so mapping this onto hidden-structure would be domain resemblance rather than coverage.

summary: A closed case-selection table for exclusion constructions, keyed on clause polarity and on whether the set excluded from is overt, returning accusative, case-by-apposition, or case-by-clause-role for the excluded item, with a parallel row set for the nominal exclusion words and their genitive complement.
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog unit for accusative roles assumes the accusative is the outcome, whereas this construction can yield nominative, accusative or genitive from the same exclusion word, and the deciding factors are clause-level polarity and antecedent presence rather than a lexical governor, so neither the accusative-role unit nor the general governance unit encodes the decision

summary: given the categorial class of the first element of a conditional response, decide whether the response connective is required, forbidden or optional, and which operator then assigns the response verb its mood
why_existing_insufficient: a general conditionals unit states that conditionals impose jussive marking; it does not encode the opener-to-connective licensing map or the locality rule that overrides jussive marking inside the response

summary: given a verb stem class and its suffix shape, decide which jussive exponent should surface and whether a weak letter is deleted, shortened or retained
why_existing_insufficient: the conditionals unit is syntactic and the weak-class unit is morphological; the selection table sits across the two and is what a per-occurrence checker actually needs

summary: A licensing table for the quantity word covering its interrogative and non-interrogative uses, returning the required form of the counted noun in each and the effect of a preceding governing particle.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 covers particles with several functions and u-n03 covers government generally, but the counted-noun form after this word is a construction-specific requirement with conditions the general governance unit does not encode, and getting it wrong changes both the case and the number of the following noun.

summary: A discriminator that first applies the literal-possibility test to separate this figure from metaphor, then routes a surviving case into one of three subtypes by whether the target of allusion is a quality, an entity, or an attribution through a possession, with the required inference chain recorded as evidence.
why_existing_insufficient: No catalogue unit addresses figure classification, and the phenomenon is idiom-level lexical semantics with no case, agreement or governance footprint that any sarf or nahw unit could carry.

summary: A discriminator for the shared written shape covering its statement-negation, prohibitive and categorical-negation functions, keyed on the following word's category and mood or case, with an explicit undecidable outcome when the disambiguating vowel is absent.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 covers multifunction particles with a different exemplar and u-n03 covers government abstractly; neither provides a per-occurrence decision for this shape nor records the very common case where the evidence needed to decide is simply not present in the text, which is precisely the situation an annotator must be able to report honestly.

summary: Item-specific licensing table for the complement of the fixed singling-out expression: complement type (definite noun / indefinite noun / clause) keyed to the set of licensed cases, the analysis attached to each case, and the status switch of the compound's suffixed element.
why_existing_insufficient: No catalog unit covers this compound. The governance unit describes case assignment generally but carries no item-level entry for a compound that licenses a case set rather than a unique case, and the multifunction-particle unit is scoped to ما.

summary: split the adversative item into a coordinating reading and an abrogator reading using pronoun attachment and the nun shape as discriminators
why_existing_insufficient: the abrogator unit lists this item as a family member unconditionally, so a coordinating occurrence would be scored against a case pattern that does not apply to it

summary: paradigm and temporal licensing of the frozen family member: no imperfective stem, person/number inflection only, present-time force only, and a named substitution route when past-time negation is intended
why_existing_insufficient: u-n02 and inc-nawasikh record the item purely as a roster member carrying the kana case signature; neither states its paradigm gap nor its temporal restriction, so a consumer has no basis to reject a past-time reading or to flag an impossible imperfective form

summary: Registry of formally unmarked nouns that license feminine concord, each with its licensing route, its semantic cluster, and a flag for attested masculine variation.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 derives number and gender exponents from form; these items carry a gender value that no morphological rule can produce, so they need a lookup table rather than a derivation.

summary: A licensing table over non-resemblance transfer: each link with its direction, the evidence that admits it, an exclusion clause against a resemblance basis and against a coherent literal reading, and a field recording any rival elided-annexation analysis.
why_existing_insufficient: No catalogue unit covers lexical-semantic transfer. u-n09 concerns estimated syntactic elements that carry case consequences, whereas these links leave no parse footprint at all, so mapping them there would be resemblance rather than coverage.

summary: A per-token decision table that separates the accusative roles a bare indefinite noun can fill — reinforcing verbal noun, motive, state and respect-specifier — keyed on root identity with the verb, verbal-noun status, the question the noun answers, and agreement with a preceding definite noun.
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog unit covering accusative roles enumerates the roles but supplies no decision procedure, and this module teaches four roles whose surface signature is the same indefinite accusative noun after a verb, so disambiguation cannot be inherited from role enumeration alone

summary: A register-gated alternation table between the two final-ending noun classes, recording direction, trigger, the resulting case-marker type, and a provenance flag distinguishing lexical doublets from licence-generated forms.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 classifies the weak and hamzated noun classes and u-s07 holds the sound-change machinery, but neither represents a permission conditioned on register nor carries the provenance distinction that stops a constructed verse variant from entering the lexicon as a real form.

summary: A discriminator over short feminine-ended deverbal nouns deciding between single-occurrence and manner readings from the first-radical vowel, verb form class, and context, with an explicit undecidable verdict for unvowelled input and a gap list of roots lacking one member.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s04 groups verbal-noun families by template but has no mechanism for two templates that differ by one short vowel and carry different semantics, and u-s01 owns letter attribution rather than vowel-driven sense selection.

summary: A licensing table stating when a verbal noun may govern an accusative object, which nominal it demotes to genitive, and what the prepositional alternative looks like, keyed to the transitivity of the underlying verb, with an abstention where the construction is ambiguous between government and simple possession.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s04 groups verbal nouns by derivational family and u-n03 records government by verbs and particles, but neither records a nominal head that inherits verbal government, which is the specific claim that makes the accusative after a possessive construction parsable rather than an error.

summary: Decision table for mim-initial nouns, separating agent noun, patient noun, third-form verbal noun, place or time noun and instrument noun, keyed on prefix vowel, internal vowel, form class of the source verb and available vocalization, with an explicit undecidable outcome for unvocalized input.
why_existing_insufficient: the ambiguity spans u-s03, u-s04 and u-s05 at once, so no single existing unit can own it; each of those units states its own template correctly while none records which competing readings must be excluded before a mim-initial token can be classified.

capability_adjudication: capability pinned by merge adjudication: three source lessons proposed three different families for one verb-class x mood -> exponent table; discriminator_table matches the inc-negation consumer that already reads mood evidence
summary: A verb-class by mood matrix giving, for each of the vowel-exponed, nun-bearing, weak-final and fixed-shape classes, the expected exponent in each mood, together with the cells where the exponent is a deletion and therefore not directly readable from the surface.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 holds the case and mood system at the level of categories but has no slot-by-slot exponent table, which is precisely what stops mood from being read off a final vowel

summary: Closed licensing table over mood governors: each entry pairs a governing token, or a host licensing an unwritten governor, with the mood it imposes and the sense required for the government to hold. This lesson supplies the third-mood half of that table.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 demands a named governor and u-n03 names government abstractly, but nothing in the catalog holds the actual inventory, the mood each member imposes, or the governing-versus-non-governing sense split that decides whether a matched token governs at all.

summary: Decision table for imperfect forms whose mood exponent is a deletion and therefore shared between two moods, keyed on the licensor in the left context, with an explicit abstention branch when no licensor is identifiable.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 records mood plus governor once both are known and u-n06 covers conditionals as a construction, but neither states that a class of surfaces is mood-ambiguous by construction nor forces abstention when the licensor is missing.

summary: given an addressed noun, decide which of the five types it belongs to and therefore whether it carries fixed marking or accusative marking, using definiteness, referential specificity and the case of any dependent element as inputs
why_existing_insufficient: the case-and-mood unit assigns case from governors; here the ending follows from a construction-internal classification, and a per-occurrence checker would otherwise mislabel a fixed damma as nominative

summary: A licensing table stating, for a clause containing more than one abrogator, which head governs which component, with clause bracketing as the input and an explicit abstention when the bracketing is ambiguous.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n02 records the per-family case signatures and u-n10 records attachment and scope generally, but neither states which head is responsible for a case when several heads are stacked, which is the claim this lesson actually adds.

summary: an ordered discrimination among the three abrogator regimes from surface cues — governor word class, presence of a separate nominative agent, and count of governed nominals — applied before any case expectation is emitted, with an explicit branch for a lemma that belongs to two families
why_existing_insufficient: inc-nawasikh keys its expectation on a flat membership lookup, which is sound only while rosters are disjoint and each sentence has one governor; it has no rule for a lemma appearing in two families and no rule for scoping two governors in one span, both of which this lesson exhibits directly

summary: per-member licensing conditions inside the verbal abrogator family: which members require a preceding negator or equivalent licenser to carry their family sense, which negating particles are interchangeable, and which member selects a subordinating particle instead of a negating one
why_existing_insufficient: inc-nawasikh lists these members as bare strings with no precondition, so a consumer would apply the family expectation to an unlicensed occurrence and to a subordinating occurrence alike, and would also silently miss the members absent from its roster

summary: Ownership and derivation rules for the relational suffix: the final geminated yaa together with its preceding kasra belongs to the affix layer and never to the root; the base's final feminine marker is deleted and certain final long vowels are dropped or converted before suffixation; agreement tails stack outside the suffix; and tokens whose base is unrecoverable abstain rather than receiving a root reading.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s01 lists yaa in its augment inventory but treats affix ownership generically. It has no rule deleting the base's final feminine marker, no account of the base-alteration cases, and no procedure for stacking agreement tails on top of a derivational suffix, so a relational token can pass its checks while still receiving a root that swallows the suffix.

summary: Closed inventory of pre-verbal tokens that precede an imperfect without licensing any mood change, so that adjacency alone can never be promoted into a government claim.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 requires a named governor before a mood claim but supplies no negative list; without one, any adjacent particle is a candidate governor and the indicative residue cannot be defended.

summary: Licensing table keyed on numeral value and on the gender of the counted noun's singular, fixing the numeral form, the number and case of the counted noun, and the genitive exponent used.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 covers noun number and gender morphology but not the inverse-agreement licensing that holds between a numeral and its counted noun, nor the construct consequences for case.

summary: given an imperfect verb ending in nun, decide whether that nun is the indicative mood exponent, and therefore deletable under a governor, or the feminine-plural agreement marker, which never alternates
why_existing_insufficient: the inflection-layering and number-and-gender units describe the suffixes but do not encode the decision that keeps a parser from assigning mood to a feminine-plural nun or from restoring a deleted nun on the wrong stem

summary: which word-final graphemes license and which block the written supporting alif of the a-form of nunation, plus the ban on co-occurrence of nunation with the definite article
why_existing_insufficient: the case and mood unit covers the values and their assignment, not the orthographic realization of the endings nor the grapheme-conditioned support rule, which is a separate closed-set decision

summary: Table pairing each oath particle with the class of element it may govern, the case it imposes, and the set of well-formed sworn-content patterns keyed on polarity and on the tense or clause type of the content, including the emphasis suffix requirement for affirmative future content and its exclusion under negation.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 records that a governor assigns a case but carries no notion of a construction whose second clause must match a pattern selected by the head particle; u-s09 supplies the emphasis suffix as an exponent but cannot say when it is licensed or barred.

summary: a closed two-way classification of letters by whether they attach leftward, plus the derived segmentation of a word into connected runs
why_existing_insufficient: every catalog unit operates above the grapheme layer; none encodes attachment behaviour, positional variants, or run segmentation, yet these determine what a surface form looks like

summary: A lexeme-keyed register of which inflectional cells exist and which are lexically blocked, so that generation, drill selection, and form validation consult an explicit block list instead of completing a paradigm by template analogy.
why_existing_insufficient: The sarf units in the catalog derive forms from root and template and treat absent forms as phonological outcomes of weakness or assimilation; none of them can record that a perfectly well-formed template cell is simply absent from the language for a given lexeme.

summary: A discriminator that decides whether a mid-clause span is a parenthetical insert or a genuine predicate, keyed on the removability test, the position between subject and predicate, and the invocation-formula content typical of such spans.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n10 covers attachment and scope and u-n12 covers cohesion, but neither supplies a positive test for a syntactically detachable interrupting span, which is exactly what prevents the misattachment this lesson warns about.

summary: A per-stem-class table of passive vocalization for perfect and imperfect, covering sound, middle-weak, final-weak and geminate stems and augmented stems, with an explicit abstention when the surface is unvocalized.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s02 classifies derived stems by augment and u-s06 classifies roots by weakness, but neither records voice as a cross-cutting vocalization dimension, and u-s07 covers the weak-letter changes without tying them to a voice template.

summary: The realisation layer between assigned inflection and observed surface form: which endings are audible in which delivery mode, the three ending-change tables, the accusative indefinite exception, and the resulting rule that absence of an ending is not evidence of absence of case.
why_existing_insufficient: the case and mood unit models assignment, not realisation, and would otherwise license the inference that an unmarked token is caseless; the clitic and inflection layering unit concerns attached elements rather than delivery-conditioned neutralisation

summary: Maps a perfect verb ending, together with the vowel state of the preceding radical, to a unique person-number-gender cell, and flags the cells that are indistinguishable without vocalisation.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers clitic and inflection layering in general but carries no cell-by-cell ending table for the perfect and no explicit ambiguity set for unvocalised text

summary: A discriminator deciding, for a perfective verb from an enumerated invocation set with a divine-name subject, whether the clause is optative or past-referring, keyed on subject identity, lemma membership and the presence of a past-time adverbial; abstains outside the enumerated set.
why_existing_insufficient: No catalog unit maps a verb form to a non-default temporal or modal reading; the sarf units classify templates and the nahw units classify case, mood and structure, none of which records this form-to-force override.

summary: Discriminates a second-order plural built on a broken plural from a first plural built on the singular and from an unrelated broken plural of the same singular, and records the closed list of licensed items together with the grouping-or-category reading the extra layer contributes.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 treats number as a single alternation between singular, dual, and plural; it has no representation for a plural serving as a derivational base, no closed-list licensing, and no semantic operator attached to a second layer.

summary: A register-gated inventory of sanctioned verse-only deviations, each with its trigger (meter or rhyme), its direction of change, its acceptance level, and an explicit statement that the syntactic parse is computed from the prose source form.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 covers case and nunation as a system and u-s07 covers sound-change machinery, but neither encodes register as an activation condition nor holds a named inventory of permissions whose whole point is that they must not fire outside verse.

summary: assignment of a token to the naming, action or residual class, with the per-class positive definitions and the mapping that blocks importing English categories; this lesson contributes the class definitions and the mapping, while L1.M2.05 to L1.M2.07 contribute the sign inventories
why_existing_insufficient: every catalog unit presupposes a class assignment without stating one: u-s01 and u-s09 assume a stem's class before ownership and layering, and u-n01 assumes it before case or mood, but no unit holds the discriminator that produces the class label

summary: A licensing table for the frozen praise and blame construction covering which subject types are admissible, which items incorporate their subject, when the specifier may be omitted, and the case of the specifier, with both classical analyses recorded as attributed alternatives rather than resolved.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n11 stores rival analyses and u-n08 stores deleted structure, but neither encodes the slot-admissibility conditions specific to this construction, and u-n03 covers government without recording that these governors are invariant.

summary: Decision table assigning a comment span to one of three realisations — single word, preposition or adverb phrase, or clause — from features of the comment's head, its word count, and the case behaviour of its internal members.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 assigns case to a comment once its realisation is known and u-s08 supplies agreement exponents, but neither decides which of the three realisations an occurrence instantiates, and the case expectations differ sharply between them.

summary: Decision table separating an adjacent nominal pair that constitutes a predication from one that is an attributive phrase or an annexation, keyed on definiteness mismatch, case marking on both members, and the absence of an intervening governor.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n01 records which slots carry which case once the slots are known, but nothing in the catalog decides whether two adjacent nominals form a predication at all; that decision is prior to case assignment and is what this lesson actually teaches.

summary: Per-preposition table of senses with the complement-type and predicate-class features that select each sense, plus the paraphrase test that confirms it.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 is scoped to a different multifunction particle, and u-n03 covers government rather than the semantic distinctions that arise under identical government.

summary: The orthography-to-pronunciation rewrite set required before any weight can be assigned: indefinite endings realised as a closing nasal, article assimilation before coronal letters, restoration of unwritten long vowels, feminine-ending treatment, silent-letter deletion and rhyme-position lengthening, together with the weight-assignment rule over voweled and quiescent consonants.
why_existing_insufficient: the catalogued phonological unit covers root-level alternation and substitution inside derivation, whereas these rules are surface-form rewrites that apply to fully inflected tokens irrespective of their morphology, and their output is a syllable-weight string that no registered capability consumes

summary: Selector mapping the tense class of the verb following the particle to its primary reading, keeping the two context-conditioned secondary readings separate and recording that no mood consequence follows.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 is scoped to a different particle and no existing unit encodes a sense selector keyed on the morphology of the following token.

summary: complement-count licensing for cognition verbs: which roster members always absorb a predication, which do so only in a judgemental sense, and what must be established about the second complement before the two-accusative expectation is asserted
why_existing_insufficient: inc-nawasikh lists these verbs as flat roster members, so a consumer would assert a two-accusative expectation for every occurrence, producing false positives on exactly the frequent literal uses this lesson isolates; the increment also has no abstention reason covering a sense-dependent gate

summary: A template class for four-radical stems covering the base and reflexive patterns, their conjugation vowels, verbal nouns and participles, the notational convention for a fourth radical slot, and the decision rule separating this class from the triliteral doubling form.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s02 is scoped to the base-through-s-t triliteral series and u-s01 assumes three radical slots when assigning letter ownership, so neither can represent a stem with four radicals; a classifier restricted to those units will assign a wrong root to every member of this class.

summary: Template inventory for non-participial adjectives of stable quality, with each template's feminine and plural shape and its inflection restriction attached.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s03 owns participles only; u-s08 owns gender and number morphology generically and does not hold template-conditioned feminine shapes; no existing unit holds the non-participial adjective template inventory or the tie between template membership and restricted inflection.

summary: A licensing table mapping singular properties (template, referent humanity, final-radical class, inherent-quality versus afflicted-state semantics, lexical restriction) to the admissible rare plural templates, with an explicit lexical-fallback verdict when no condition resolves.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s08 carries number morphology as such and u-s06 carries radical classes, but neither holds the conditional table that decides among competing plural templates for one singular, and the semantic licensing filter has no representation at all.

summary: Ordered pipeline resolving an unpointed consonant skeleton by applying particle category filters, then syntactic-role case prediction, then pattern matching, then a semantic coherence check, recording which filter decided the reading.
why_existing_insufficient: the individual units supply the case system, particle behaviour, and the pattern inventory separately; none states the order in which they apply or what to do when two of them conflict.

summary: Decision table selecting concord exponents for adjectives, verbs, pronouns and demonstratives from referent rationality, number, plural type and verb-subject order, listing permitted alternates rather than a single answer.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n10 covers attachment, scope and referent resolution but carries no rationality feature, and u-s08 is morphological; nothing in the catalog encodes the rationality-driven concord decision or the alternates it licenses.

summary: Records, per register, the co-occurring feature bundle (clause completeness, voice, connector class, rhyme, annexation depth, formula density, tone, goal) as teaching material, explicitly marked non-executable until a passage-level classifier exists.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n12 owns discourse cohesion devices as grammatical objects; a register taxonomy is a text-type judgement over whole passages, which no unit in the catalog is scoped to hold.

summary: a feature checklist that registers or dates a text span - dual productivity, energetic nun, realised case, particle rigour, constituent order, adverbial accusative versus preposition - and states, per register, whether the case exponent or the constituent order carries the functional load
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog encodes phenomena but indexes none of them to a register or period; without such a table a parser applies classical governance expectations to a text that does not realise them, and treats pausal delivery as missing inflection

summary: A discriminator that, at a reporting boundary, decides whether a person, place or time deictic inside the reported clause is anchored to the reporter or to the original speaker, using the reporting verb, the complementizer and the clause boundary as evidence, and abstains where the discourse participants are not recoverable.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n10 resolves referents inside a single anchoring situation and u-n12 handles cohesion across sentences, but neither models a second speech situation embedded under a reporting head, which is what makes the pronoun ambiguous here.

summary: a closed comparison of the syntactic carriers of restriction - argument fronting, the compound restrictive particle, and negation plus exception - each paired with the emphasis it contributes and the structural signature that identifies it
why_existing_insufficient: no catalog unit treats restriction as an effect with multiple carriers; u-n07 covers the polyfunctionality of one particle, not the set of devices that produce exclusivity

summary: The production-direction method for restriction: transform a general proposition into a restricted one, select the device by register, place the target in the focused slot, and state the implicit negation before accepting the result. Retained as a drill and drafting rubric, not as a projection capability.
why_existing_insufficient: The linguistic facts belong to the units credited at L5.M1.06 and L5.M1.07; what is new here is a composition and analysis procedure, which no consumer-backed capability family represents.

summary: a marker-to-move table for classical commentary prose - lemma marker, gloss markers, justification markers, and layer-attribution formulas - allowing a reader or an extractor to segment a commentary into quoted base text, interpretation, and evidence
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog covers syntactic phenomena inside sentences; nothing covers the discourse format of the annotation layer, and u-n12 concerns cohesion within ordinary running text rather than the marker grammar of a commentary

summary: the three short-vowel marks with their placement rules, plus the fully/partially/un-vocalized state of a token and what each state licenses
why_existing_insufficient: no catalog unit represents the diacritic layer or the vocalization state of a surface form, although every sarf and nahw unit implicitly assumes vowels are known

summary: Classifies suffix-built abstract nouns: admissible base categories, obligatory feminine ending, and separation from the plain relational adjective sharing the same suffix minus that ending.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s04 covers verbal-noun families derived from verbs; this formation derives from nouns and adjectives and is barred from verbal bases, so it does not belong to that unit's licensing.

summary: A licensing table over verbs stating whether either exclamatory template may be built directly, keyed to root letter count, frozen status, derived-adjective pattern and gradability, with the periphrastic repair recorded as the licensed alternative and an abstention where gradability is undetermined.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 covers government generally and u-n04 covers accusative-taking positions, but neither records a per-verb admissibility test for a fixed template, and no existing unit pairs a blocked construction with its licensed repair.

summary: A discriminator deciding, for a particle standing between a mental-state verb and a following clause, whether it blocks the verb's case assignment or instead packages the clause as the verb's complement.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 handles particles with several functions but not this specific blocking-versus-complementising split, and u-n03 has no representation for a governor whose assignment is interrupted.

summary: A discriminator separating the specification role from the circumstantial accusative, the direct object and the genitive complement, keyed to trigger type, definiteness, case and the question the noun answers, with the subtype split recorded.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n04 enumerates the accusative roles but supplies no decision procedure for choosing among them at a given occurrence, and u-s08 covers numeral and gender morphology without the complement-case consequences that separate the quantifier readings.

summary: A discriminator separating shared-argument contention from ordinary coordination and from single-governor displacement, and emitting the two school-attributed governor assignments with the pronoun each requires.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n11 stores that schools disagree but holds no executable discriminator for detecting this configuration, and u-n03 assumes a single resolvable governor per argument.

summary: A discriminator over generic and third-person frames that asks whether a specific discourse participant is the intended target, listing the carrier frames and the situational evidence each one needs.
why_existing_insufficient: The genuinely new material for u-n10 is narrow: a generic relative head may have a specific individual as its intended referent, fixed pragmatically rather than syntactically, and u-n12 gains the observation that such frames bind to a participant across turns. The frame inventory and the social-function account have no home in the catalogue, and u-n11 is touched only because the classical status of the device is itself disputed.

summary: A discriminator over comparison configurations: four named slots, two binary parameters (exponent present or absent, shared quality verbalised or not), the composite labels they generate, and the exponent inventory with the case each exponent licenses.
why_existing_insufficient: No catalogue unit covers rhetorical figure classification; the only genuine overlap with u-n02 and u-n03 is the governance fact about the كأنّ frame and the prefixed particle, which is a small licensing addition and leaves the slot-and-type scheme homeless.

summary: Decision table for adjacent identical tokens: routes a pair to emphatic repetition, to coordination, or to a no-decision outcome, keyed on the presence of an intervening coordinator, inflectional identity, whether the second token fills an independent slot, and a discourse check for disfluency or enumeration.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n12 treats cohesion across a discourse, but the question this lesson raises is a local one, namely whether an adjacent identical pair is a licensed follower at all; no catalog unit supplies that reject path, and without it any repetition detector would over-fire.

summary: Licensing table for the meaning-word emphasis follower: closed lexical inventory, the obligatory coindexed clitic keyed to head phi-features, case copying, plural shape substitution, and the dual pair with its two case shapes, plus an explicit reject rule for the same lexemes used as annexation heads.
why_existing_insufficient: u-s09 covers clitic and inflection layering as morphology and u-n01 assigns case per slot, but neither states when a following nominal is licensed as an emphasis follower, and nothing in the catalog separates these lexemes in their follower use from their far more common annexation-head use.

summary: A valency table for the causative informing and showing verbs, listing three ordered accusative slots with their roles, the non-causative base of each verb, and the admissible realisations of each slot as noun, clitic or detached pronoun.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n04 enumerates accusative categories without valency frames, u-n03 has no multi-slot argument representation, and u-s02 records derived stems without linking a stem change to a change in complement count.

summary: the joint conditions under which a string counts as a complete analysable utterance, and the fragment classes that fail each condition, including the unresolved case of an incorporated subject
why_existing_insufficient: no catalog unit states when a span is an utterance at all; u-n12 handles cohesion between already-complete sentences and u-n08 handles estimated material inside them, so neither supplies the entry threshold

summary: A licensing table over verbal valency: default frame, the conditions under which a bare accusative object is admitted outside that frame, the conditions separating recoverable omission from rhetorical withholding, and the school attribution attached to each reading.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 and u-n04 cover government and accusative complements as they stand, and u-n11 holds rival analyses, but none of them represents a verb frame as a defeasible licensing condition with register and recoverability as the defeaters.

summary: A lexical licensing table pairing verbs with the genitive-governing particle they select, so that a sense-and-attachment decision can be made from the verb rather than from the particle's default gloss.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n03 encodes government abstractly and u-n07 covers particles with several functions, but neither stores the per-verb selection facts that decide which particle is grammatical and what relation it then expresses; without that table the multi-sense particle entries have no way to be narrowed at an occurrence.

summary: an ordered analysis routine for reading a fully vocalized word and an ordered production routine for writing one, with per-stage checkpoints
why_existing_insufficient: the catalog models tables and classifications, not ordered procedures; this lesson's yield is a staged method that no listed unit and no consumer family currently represents

summary: classify a surface verb as active or passive from its vowel melody, per derived form and per stem class, and mark the cells whose consonant skeleton is voice-ambiguous when unvocalised
why_existing_insufficient: u-s02 lists the derived forms without a voice dimension and u-s07 handles weak-letter changes rather than melodies; nothing in the catalog can currently answer whether a given surface is active or passive, or say when that question is undecidable from the letters

summary: A discriminator table for the senses of the connective waw — coordination, accompaniment, state, oath, and parenthetical insertion — keyed on the case of the following nominal, the presence of a verbal governor, the definiteness and role saturation of the preceding nominal, and the presence of a linking pronoun.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n07 is scoped to a different multifunction item; u-n04 is a role inventory rather than a decision table; u-n10 covers scope and referent but not sense selection on this token. Lessons 2, 3 and 4 of this module each turn on a different sense of the same connective with no shared discriminator between them.

summary: check that a surface form produced by a root carrying more than one weak radical is consistent with the ordered composition of the applicable rules, rather than with either rule applied alone
why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 enumerates weak classes as disjoint categories and u-s07 states rules in isolation; a stem that qualifies for two of them has no consistency check anywhere in the catalog, and these are precisely the surfaces where a wrong single-rule output is still a well-formed-looking word

summary: Per-item table for adverbials of time and place recording, for each member of the closed inventory, whether it is declined or built, whether it obligatorily heads an annexation, what happens when its dependent is omitted, and whether it may itself be governed by a preposition — the facts that decide when an accusative exponent is actually expected and when the case is positional only.
why_existing_insufficient: u-n04 discriminates the accusative roles from one another but starts from the assumption that a nasb marking has already been read; it holds no lexeme inventory. u-n01 records that built words carry positional case as a general exception but does not say which adverbials are built. Neither prevents the lesson's blanket accusative rule from being projected onto items that never show the exponent.
